# Risk rules for pull requests (issue #211). The one place these paths live.
#
# CI's `risk-gate` check labels every PR risk:high, risk:medium or risk:low from the paths it
# changes. The label shows how careful to be; it does not block a merge (#240). The check passes
# for every tier and fails only if it cannot read the PR or set the label.
#
# One rule per line: `high <pattern>` or `low <pattern>`.
#   - A pattern ending in `/` is a folder: it matches everything under it.
#   - A pattern with no `/` matches the file name at any depth (`*.md` = every Markdown file).
#   - Any other pattern is matched against the full path; `*` may cross folders.
# A file is high if any high rule matches it, else low if any low rule matches, else medium.
# A PR takes the highest tier of its files; a moved file counts under its old and new names.
#
# The checker always reads this file from the branch the PR merges into (main), never from the
# PR itself, so a PR cannot change the rules it is judged by. Changes here land like any other
# change to .github/: as risk:high.

high src/gct/grounder/
high src/gct/providers/
high .github/
# Desktop move (#216, rules from #218): the library and search replace db.py and migrations/,
# and the desktop main process and preload hold the window's security settings. Desktop
# screens (desktop/renderer/ and the like) stay medium.
high src/gct/library/
high src/gct/search/
high desktop/main*
high desktop/preload*

low docs/
low design/
low *.md
low tests/
